Resolves #21071

A `Neo.dialog.Base` can now animate out of any node: a list item, a grid cell, or a menu row. `animateShow()` and `animateHide()` read the window and app from the target only when the target is a component; any other node leaves the dialog in the `windowId` and `appName` it was created with. Previously both methods dereferenced `Neo.getComponent(animateTargetId)` unconditionally, so a non-component target threw on the first line. The animation geometry was never the problem, because it comes from `getDomRect()`, which works for any node. This also drops `animateShow()`'s `appName` local, which was assigned and never read.

The web desktop (#21064) needs this so that a launcher icon, which is a list item, can be the window's spawn point.

Evidence: L2 (unit tests run the real `animateShow()` and `animateHide()` with the main-thread reads stubbed; red on `dev` with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'windowId')`, green after) → L2 required (both ACs are dialog-state contracts). No residuals.

| AC-2 a component target keeps today's behavior | CI: same spec, "a component target still moves the dialog into the window and app of that component"; `Visibility.spec.mjs` stays green |
| AC-3 `npm run test-unit` green | CI: unit job (full local run: 7415 passed, 2 skipped) |

### 🔬 Depth Floor

- **Challenge**: Non-blocking lifecycle edge case for ephemeral non-component targets: unlike persistent button components, a non-component `animateTargetId` (`list.Base` launcher item filtered out on account switch in `#21064`, or a virtualized grid cell scrolled out of view) can leave the DOM while the dialog is open. On `animateHide()`, `DomAccess#getBoundingClientRect` (`src/main/DomAccess.mjs:524-547`) returns `{}` rather than throwing, so `closeOrHide(false)` still completes after 250ms, but the second `applyDeltas` step writes `undefinedpx` styles during that 250ms window instead of skipping straight to `closeOrHide(false)`. Animation changes are out of scope for `#21071`, so worth watching in `#21064`/`#21073` when switching demo accounts with an open window. Also verified `src/timeline/EventEditor.mjs:133-135` (`Neo.getComponent(this.animateTargetId) || this.owner || this`): keeping `|| this.owner` there remains load-bearing because `scheduler.Container` caches a single `EventEditor` across opens, whereas its trailing `|| this` was only guarding the pre-`#21072` null dereference.
